To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
adolescents living in higher-risk neighborhoods were more likely to use substances, and this was mediated by their willingness to use and their risk images.

(1) risk cognitions mediate the relation between risk contexts and adolescent use, (2) risk cognitions are a function of context, (3) context moderates the relation between willingness to use and adolescent use, and (4) context does not moderate the relation between intentions to use and adolescent substance use.

the risk cognitions of adolescents living in high- risk neighborhoods are more likely to be associated with actual risk behaviors, and this relation is stronger than the relation for adolescents living in low-risk neighborhoods.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how adolescents’ risk cognitons are shaped by their environment and how these cognitions influence their use.
the role of cognitions in the development of substance use among adolescents.
the role of cognitions in mediating and moderating the impact of contextual factors on adolescent substance use.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the context of high-risk neighborhoods does not moderate the relation between risk cognitions (risk images, willingness to try substances, and intentions to try substances) and substance use, but it does moderate the relation between willingness to use and substance use.
context affects substance use through adolescents’ risk cogniti ons, but that the relation between intentions to use and use does not vary by context.
context affects adolescent substance use by influencing the adolescents’ cognitions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
context effects on adolescent substance use are mediated through risk cognitions, but the relation between willingness to use and use is moderated by context.
context is important for understanding the cognitions that lead adolescents to use substances.
the cognitions that mediate the impact on context on adolescent substance abuse are the risk images and willingness to use.
The main takeaway from our work is that
risk cognitions are a key mechanism through which context affects adolescent substance use.
context matters for adolescents’ risk behaviors.
the context of adolescents’ lives is important to consider when trying to understand their risk cognitions and behaviors. (PsycINFO Database Record (c) 2019 APA, all rights reserved)
